title: Finite closed fibre of a purely inseparable integral closure
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $K$ its fraction field, and $L/K$ a finite purely inseparable field extension [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] in characteristic a prime $p$. Let $x\in R$ and suppose $R/xR$ is a domain and N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]. Writing $S$ for the integral closure [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] of $R$ in $L$, the module $S/xS$ is finite [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] over $R/xR$. No completeness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: If x=0, identify R/xR with R and their fraction fields. Its N-2 hypothesis gives finiteness of S in L, hence finiteness of the asserted quotient. For x nonzero carry out the following steps.

*An exponent $q$ and the enlargement of $L$ (the details of 'by enlarging $L$ if necessary').* Let $b_1,\dots,b_m$ be a $K$-basis of $L$; by [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] there are $e_i\ge0$ with $b_i^{p^{e_i}}\in K$. Put $e=\max_ie_i$ and $q=p^e$; then $b_i^q=(b_i^{p^{e_i}})^{p^{e-e_i}}\in K$, and since $\alpha\mapsto\alpha^q$ is the iterated Frobenius, a ring endomorphism of $L$ [def-weil-ring-frobenius], every $\alpha=\sum c_ib_i$ ($c_i\in K$) has $\alpha^q=\sum c_i^qb_i^q\in K$: $L^q\subseteq K$. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $L$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $y\in\Omega$ with $y^q=x$ (a root of the nonconstant polynomial $T^q-x$). Let $L'=L(y)\subseteq\Omega$ be the subfield generated by $L$ and $y$; $y$ is algebraic over $L$, so $L'/L$ is finite [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension], and $L'/K$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity]. The ring $L[y]$ is a finite-dimensional $L$-algebra contained in a field, hence a domain in which multiplication by a nonzero element is an injective, so surjective, $L$-linear endomorphism; so $L[y]$ is a field and $L'=L[y]$. Thus every element of $L'$ is $\sum_ia_iy^i$ with $a_i\in L$, and its $q$-th power is $\sum_ia_i^qx^i\in K$. Hence $L'/K$ is finite purely inseparable with $L'^q\subseteq K$, and $L'$ contains $y$ with $y^q=x$. If $S'$ is the integral closure of $R$ in $L'$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], the integral closure of $R$ in $L$ is $S'\cap L$, an $R$-submodule of $S'$; so if $S'$ is a finitely generated $R$-module, so is $S'\cap L$, by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] ($R$ Noetherian). Replacing $L$ by $L'$ we may and do assume: $L^q\subseteq K$ and there is $y\in L$ with $y^q=x$. Let $S$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $L$. For the desired quotient rather than S itself, the inclusion S into the enlarged closure T induces S/xS into T/xT: S intersect xT = xS, since a/x lies in L and is integral whenever a lies in S intersect xT.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032P (lemma-tate-japanese, lines 45534-45589), proof: 'Let q be a power of p such that L^q ⊂ K. By enlarging L if necessary we may assume there exists an element y ∈ L such that y^q = x'

proof.text: *Basic properties of $S$.* $S$ is a subring of $L$ containing $R$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], hence a domain, and by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal] $L$ is a fraction field of $S$. (a) For $f\in S$ we have $f^q\in R$: $f^q\in L^q\subseteq K$ is integral over $R$ (a power of an integral element; $S$ is a ring), and $R$ is integrally closed in $K$ by (1) [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. (b) $y\in S$, being a root of the monic $T^q-x\in R[T]$, and $y\neq0$ since $y^q=x\neq0$. (c) $xS\cap R=xR$: if $r=xs$ with $r\in R$, $s\in S$, then $s=r/x\in K$ is integral over $R$, so $s\in R$ by normality.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032P (lemma-tate-japanese, lines 45534-45589), proof: implicit in 'It is clear that q = {f ∈ S | f^q ∈ p} = yS since y^q = x' and in 'an element in the intersection has qth power contained in ∩x^nR'

proof.text: *The prime $\mathfrak q=yS$ over $\mathfrak p$ (the source's 'it is clear').* Put $\mathfrak q=yS$. Claim: for $f\in S$, $f\in\mathfrak q\iff f^q\in\mathfrak p$. If $f=ys$ ($s\in S$) then $f^q=xs^q\in xR$ since $s^q\in R$ by step 3(a). Conversely if $f^q=xr$ with $r\in R$, then $g=f/y\in L$ satisfies $g^q=f^q/x=r\in R$, so $g$ is a root of the monic $T^q-r$ and $g\in S$, i.e. $f=yg\in yS$. Consequences: $1\notin\mathfrak q$ since $1\notin\mathfrak p$; if $fg\in\mathfrak q$ then $f^qg^q=(fg)^q\in\mathfrak p$ with $f^q,g^q\in R$, so as $\mathfrak p$ is prime $f^q\in\mathfrak p$ or $g^q\in\mathfrak p$, i.e. $f\in\mathfrak q$ or $g\in\mathfrak q$. So $\mathfrak q$ is a prime ideal of $S$. For $r\in R$: $r\in\mathfrak q\iff r^q\in\mathfrak p\iff r\in\mathfrak p$ ($\mathfrak p$ prime), so $\mathfrak q\cap R=\mathfrak p$. (The source deduces from Lemma 0BRA that $\mathfrak q$ is the unique prime over $\mathfrak p$; uniqueness is not used below, only that $yS$ is a prime lying over $\mathfrak p$, which is verified here directly.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032P (lemma-tate-japanese, lines 45534-45589), proof: 'there is a unique prime ideal q ⊂ S lying over the prime ideal p = xR. It is clear that q = {f ∈ S | f^q ∈ p} = yS since y^q = x'

proof.text: *$R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain.* $R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a local ring, a domain (a subring of $K$), and Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Height of $\mathfrak p$: by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound] with $t=1$, $f_1=x$, $J=xR=\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak P=\mathfrak p$, $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)\le\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p/J)+1=\operatorname{ht}((0)\subset R/xR)+1=1$, the zero ideal having height $0$ (a chain of primes contained in $(0)$ has only the term $(0)$). And $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)\ge1$ by the chain $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p$ ($R$ is a domain, $\mathfrak p\ne0$). By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime] the Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] of $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)=1$. (The source states here that $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a discrete valuation ring (00PD), and then that $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is Noetherian (Krull–Akizuki 00PG) and a discrete valuation ring; the rest of the proof uses only that $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain, which is what Lemma 031F asks for, so these further assertions are not needed and not stated.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032P (lemma-tate-japanese, lines 45534-45589), proof: 'Observe that R_p is a discrete valuation ring by Lemma lemma-characterize-dvr. Then S_q is Noetherian by Krull-Akizuki ... a discrete valuation ring'

proof.text: *$\kappa(\mathfrak q)/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is finite.* Since $\mathfrak q\cap R=\mathfrak p$ (step 4), $R\setminus\mathfrak p\subseteq S\setminus\mathfrak q$, so the inclusion $R\subseteq S$ extends to an injective homomorphism of domains $\varphi:R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$, both rings being subrings of $L$ ($R_{\mathfrak p}\subseteq K$). The fraction field of $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is $K$, and that of $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is $L$, as $S\subseteq S_{\mathfrak q}\subseteq L$ and $L$ is a fraction field of $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal]; $\dim_KL<\infty$. The maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$ satisfies $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak n)=\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$: if $r/s\in\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$ with $r\in R$, $s\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$, write $r/s=f/t$ with $f\in\mathfrak q$, $t\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$; then $rt=sf\in\mathfrak q$ and $t\notin\mathfrak q$ give $r\in\mathfrak q\cap R=\mathfrak p$; the other inclusion is clear. By step 5, [lem-weil-pbc-dim-one-residue-field-extensions-finite] (3) applies to $\varphi$ and $\mathfrak n$: $\kappa(\mathfrak q)=S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$ is a finite-dimensional field extension of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032P (lemma-tate-japanese, lines 45534-45589), proof: 'By Lemma lemma-finite-extension-residue-fields-dimension-1 we see that κ(q)/κ(p) is a finite field extension' (Tag 031F)

proof.text: *$S/yS$ is a finitely generated $R$-module.* By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-residue-field-algebra] (b), $R/\mathfrak p\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is injective and makes $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ a fraction field of the domain $R/\mathfrak p=R/xR$, and $S/\mathfrak q\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is injective; these maps are compatible with $R/\mathfrak p\to S/\mathfrak q$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. By step 6 and hypothesis (2) ($R/xR$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]), the integral closure $S'$ of $R/xR$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a finitely generated $R/xR$-module, hence a finitely generated $R$-module [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-over-finite-algebra] ($R/xR$ is generated by $1$ as an $R$-module). Every element of $S/\mathfrak q$ is integral over $R/\mathfrak p$ (reduce modulo $\mathfrak q$ a monic equation over $R$ of a lift in $S$), so its image lies in $S'$: $S/yS=S/\mathfrak q$ is isomorphic to an $R$-submodule of $S'$, hence finitely generated over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032P (lemma-tate-japanese, lines 45534-45589), proof: 'Hence the integral closure S' ⊂ κ(q) of R/xR is finite over R/xR by assumption (2). Since S/yS ⊂ S' this implies that S/yS is finite over R'

proof.text: *$S/xS$ is a finitely generated $R/xR$-module.* By induction on $n\ge1$, $S/y^nS$ is a finitely generated $R$-module; $n=1$ is step 7. For the induction step consider $S/yS\xrightarrow{\mu}S/y^{n+1}S\xrightarrow{\pi}S/y^nS\to0$, with $\mu(s+yS)=y^ns+y^{n+1}S$ (well defined) and $\pi$ the projection. $\pi$ is surjective, $\pi\circ\mu=0$, and $\ker\pi=y^nS/y^{n+1}S=\operatorname{im}\mu$. (Also $\mu$ is injective: $y^ns=y^{n+1}t$ gives $s=yt$ as $S$ is a domain and $y\ne0$, so $y^iS/y^{i+1}S\cong S/yS$ as in the source.) By [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-extension-of-finite] $S/y^{n+1}S$ is finitely generated over $R$. For $n=q$: $y^q=x$, so $S/xS$ is a finitely generated $R$-module; as $x$ annihilates it, the same generators generate it over $R/xR$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032P (lemma-tate-japanese, lines 45534-45589), proof: 'Note that S/y^nS has a finite filtration whose subquotients are the modules y^iS/y^{i+1}S ≅ S/yS. Hence we see that each S/y^nS is finite over R. In particular S/xS is finite over R'

proof.text: step 5 gives T/xT finite over R. The injection S/xS into T/xT from step 2 and Noetherianity give finiteness of S/xS. Its R-action factors through R/xR, and an R-generating set is therefore also an R/xR-generating set.

mathlib_searches.query: finite purely inseparable extension integral closure adic separated quotient finite complete normal domain

For a normal Noetherian domain R and a prime principal ideal xR with Japanese quotient R/xR, the reduction modulo x of the integral closure in a finite purely inseparable extension is a finite module.

lean.statement:
theorem tate_purely_inseparable_closure_quotient_finite
    (R : Type u) (K L : Type v) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
    [Algebra K L] [Algebra R L] [IsScalarTower R K L]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] (x : R) (hnormal : IsIntegrallyClosed R)
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP K p] [FiniteDimensional K L]
    [IsPurelyInseparable K L]
    [IsDomain (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({x} : Set R))]
    (hquot : IsN2 (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({x} : Set R))
      (FractionRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({x} : Set R)))) :
    Module.Finite (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({x} : Set R))
      ((integralClosure R L) ⧸
        (Ideal.span ({x} : Set R) • ⊤ : Submodule R (integralClosure R L)))
